    Calculate Global Linkage Disequilibrium Decay and Render Regression Curves

    plot_global_ld_decay.Rd

    Evaluates genome-wide linkage disequilibrium (LD) decay profiles across populations. The function automates the structural synchronization of genotype matrices and variant map arrays, filters out unanchored genomic scaffolds, processes pairwise r2 coefficients using local vectorized window blocks, trims the physical distance space to isolate decay plateaus, fits a non-linear least squares (NLS) regression model, and plots a profile.

    plot_global_ld_decay(
  geno,
  map,
  max_distance_bp = 5e+05,
  max_plot_points = 1e+05,
  r2_threshold = 0.2,
  output_image_path = "Figures/ld_short_range.png"
)

    Arguments

    geno

    A data frame or matrix of genotype dosages. Must contain a `"taxa"` column identifying individual samples, with all remaining columns containing variant IDs (scaled 0/1/2).

    map

    A data frame containing variant coordinate details. Must include columns named `"SNP"`, `"Chromosome"`, and `"Position"`.

    max_distance_bp

    Numeric. The maximum physical distance cutoff (in base-pairs) to trim the long x-axis tail and focus the visualization window on where the curve plateaus. Default is 500000 (500kb).

    max_plot_points

    Numeric. The maximum number of pairwise data points to sample and display on the final scatterplot scatter matrix to prevent system RAM memory failure. Default is 100000.

    r2_threshold

    Numeric. The base-line horizontal intercept boundary showing target LD background limits. Default is 0.2.

    output_image_path

    Character string pointing to a local file location (including file extension) to save the rendered chart asset. Set to NULL to bypass saving. Default is "Figures/ld_short_range.png".

    Value

    A list structure containing two key package elements:

    plot

    The generated composite ggplot visualization object layout configuration.

    ld_data

    A filtered data.frame holding pairwise variant physical distances (d) and linkage values (r2), excluding self-correlations.
